content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes (e.g., post-70.93 or 71.17), often overshooting by 2–5% before correcting.
- Shows persistent downward bias in the middle of the forecast (days 10–20), failing to capture mean reversion toward higher levels.
- Tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in upward trends.
- Underreacts to recent high prices (e.g., 72+), failing to anticipate mean reversion or volatility clustering.
- Overestimates volatility in low-price zones (e.g., 65–68), leading to overconfident upward forecasts.
- Corrects late in the forecast horizon (days 25–30) but often with delayed or muted response to true price spikes.
